scope: Proposition 3.7 (Strict compactness of minimizing enclosures) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-with-charge-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 84ca5bc05bc907a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let smooth metrics gj converge to g uniformly on compact sets, with common end bounds as in Lemma 3.3, and choose their auxiliary extensions to converge uniformly on the filling. If Mj ∈ Mgj (F), a subsequence converges to M ∈ Mg(F) with 1Mj −→ 1M in L1 , Pg(Mj) −→ Pg(M) = pg(F). (3.11) For every continuous function Ψ on the bundle of unoriented two-planes over the common compact truncation, Z ∂Mj Ψ(x, Tx∂Mj) dAg −→ Z ∂M Ψ(x, Tx∂M) dAg. (3.12) Thus Mg(F) is a compact metric space, and the area first-variation functional is continuous on it.
